name: R6: pairing ignores the image type
why: The key is type + comment prefix; without the type, an Other 'left' and a Sticker 'right' of the same comment become one spread.
grep: a left and a right of different types stay apart

name: R6: no duplicate guard
why: Two lefts for one key are ambiguous; pairing the first one guesses.
grep: two lefts for one key stay single pages

name: R6: Liner pages are not paged
why: Only Booklet goes to the pager; the four Liner pages land among the singles.
grep: the pager and singles hold the rest

name: R6: the pager page is not clamped
why: A page index past the end shows nothing (or throws) instead of the last page.
grep: stops at both ends

name: R6: the clamped page is not stored back
why: The last page is shown, but the stored index stays past the end, so one back step does nothing visible.
grep: stops at both ends

name: R6: a layout switch keeps the pager page
why: Coming back to Spreads should start on the first liner pages.
grep: stops at both ends

name: R6: the viewer steps through the visible tiles only
why: Collecting the on-screen tiles (as Grid does) loses the liner pages the pager hides.
grep: liner pages behind the pager included

name: R6: a stored 'spreads' layout is not accepted
why: The choice is lost: the layout falls back to Grid after the click that stored it.
grep: Spreads is offered and remembered

name: R6: the spread's own width cap
why: Without its max-width the spread is still capped by the section (calc(100vw - 32px)), so the phone check is expected to stay green: recorded, not hidden.
grep: an opened spread fits the phone window

name: R7: no one-medium rule
why: On a single medium every Medium image is certainly that medium's; without the rule five images on one medium are refused.
grep: one medium takes every Medium image

name: R7: equal counts assign even with comments
why: Archive order is a guess once any comment exists: one 'CD 3' plus two uncommented images would be placed 1, 2, 3.
grep: one readable comment among uncommented images

name: R7: equal counts never assign
why: The 'as many Medium images as media' rule the user chose: without it the uncommented 3-on-3 case is refused.
grep: as many uncommented Medium images as media

name: R7: sides counted on CDs
why: A CD has no side C; treating every medium as two-sided assigns 'side C' to CD 2.
grep: is medium 2 on vinyl, and nothing on CDs

name: R7: sides never counted
why: On vinyl, 'side C' names medium 2.
grep: is medium 2 on vinyl, and nothing on CDs

name: R7: a medium that does not exist is accepted
why: 'CD 7' on a 3-CD release names no medium; it must land in the note, not vanish into a missing h3.
grep: a comment naming a medium that does not exist

name: R7: a comment naming two media takes the first
why: 'CD 2 + CD 3' is ambiguous; the first number is a guess.
grep: a comment naming a medium that does not exist

name: R7: the thumb image takes the click
why: Without pointer-events none the click target is the IMG, which the h3's collapse handler does not exempt: clicking a thumb collapses the medium.
grep: without collapsing the medium

name: R7 mobile: the thumb image takes the tap
why: Same trap on touch: the tap's target becomes the IMG, the h3 collapse handler takes it and stops it, and the viewer never opens.
grep: tapping a Medium thumb in the medium heading

name: R7: the note opens only the first Medium image
why: The note stands for every Medium image; the viewer must step through all of them.
grep: the note opens the viewer on the Medium images only

name: R7: no repair from the filter pass
why: The thumbs ride updateFilterButtonsVisibility(); without that call an h3 rebuilt after the section loaded stays bare.
grep: the thumbs survive a filter re-render

name: R7: not applied when the record arrives
why: The first application is when the section's record loads; something else may call the filter pass after that, so this records whether that call alone is load-bearing.
grep: a note, never a guess

name: R7: the setting is ignored
why: Turning off 'Show Medium images in each medium heading' must leave the h3s alone.
grep: the setting turns them off
